item.title: Johnson Lowe Gallery Opens “Dangerous Games,” Second Solo Exhibition by Navin Norling
item.description: Navin Norling's solo exhibition, Dangerous Games, opened at Johnson Lowe Gallery, featuring works that dissect classic Americana imagery through found materials, folk traditions, and layered visual codes, and is a commentary on American history, cultural erasure, and the political moment. The post Johnson Lowe Gallery Opens “Dangerous Games,” Second Solo Exhibition by Navin Norling appeared first on The Atlanta Voice.

item.title: What we know about why the US and Israel attacked Iran and Tehran’s retaliation
item.description: The US and Israel have launched a joint military operation against Iran, killing Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and sparking a conflict that could draw in much of the Middle East. The post What we know about why the US and Israel attacked Iran and Tehran’s retaliation appeared first on The Atlanta Voice.

item.title: Only the Four Black male candidates show up for Democratic governors forum in Clayton County
item.description: Four Black men running for Georgia's top seat, along with a Black moderator and invocation, took part in a gubernatorial forum in Clayton County, the seventh-largest county in Georgia, hosted by the Clayton County Democratic Party and the Young Democrats of Clayton County. The post Only the Four Black male candidates show up for Democratic governors forum in Clayton County appeared first on The Atlanta Voice.

item.title: Atlanta Hawks and Chase Bank host third annual Rookie Entrepreneur Program
item.description: Ten Georgia-based small business owners gathered for the third annual Rookie Entrepreneur Community Program, a partnership between the Atlanta Hawks and JPMorgan Chase, to receive financial tools and guidance to scale their businesses. The post Atlanta Hawks and Chase Bank host third annual Rookie Entrepreneur Program appeared first on The Atlanta Voice.

item.title: Meet Ashleigh Pearson, the chocolatier making fine dining chocolates accessible
item.description: Ashleigh Pearson, one of the few Black women chocolatiers in the country, has created Avec Noelle to make fine confections accessible to everyone, using her expertise in pastry and chocolate making to create nostalgic, community-focused bonbons. The post Meet Ashleigh Pearson, the chocolatier making fine dining chocolates accessible appeared first on The Atlanta Voice.

item.title: ‘I Can Win This’: A Black woman qualifies to run in Georgia Secretary of State race
item.description: Penny Brown Reynolds and Kelvin King are running to be the first Black Secretary of State in Georgia, with Adrian Consonery, Jr. also running for the Democratic seat, and the voters will decide if a Black Georgia Secretary of State will be elected. The post ‘I Can Win This’: A Black woman qualifies to run in Georgia Secretary of State race appeared first on The Atlanta Voice.

item.description: The war in Sudan has killed tens of thousands and displaced over 11 million people, with the international community largely ignoring the crisis and foreign powers fueling the conflict. item.title: Meeting to determine US measles elimination status pushed back to November
item.description: The international meeting to determine the status of measles elimination in the US has been delayed until November to allow for a thorough and transparent assessment of the 2025 measles outbreaks. The post Meeting to determine US measles elimination status pushed back to November appeared first on The Atlanta Voice.

item.title: FIFA is back in Atlanta with 100 Days till World Cup 2026 begins
item.description: FIFA World Cup 2026 is set to kick off in 100 days, and FIFA held a team workshop in Atlanta to prepare for the tournament, featuring presentations on technology, logistics, and fan experiences. The post FIFA is back in Atlanta with 100 Days till World Cup 2026 begins appeared first on The Atlanta Voice.

item.title: Scientists discover a key to staying mentally sharp in old age
item.description: SuperAgers, people over 80 with superior memories, have twice the number of young neurons as cognitively healthy adults and 2.5 times as many as people with Alzheimer's disease, suggesting that the aging brain has the capacity to regenerate. The post Scientists discover a key to staying mentally sharp in old age appeared first on The Atlanta Voice.
